sections.h2: Where is Urbandale, and which counties does it straddle?
sections.html:
Urbandale is a suburb on the northwest side of the Des Moines metro, and it lies in both Polk and Dallas counties. That split matters for sellers, since the county that bills your property tax depends on which side of the line your house sits.

The city covers about 22.5 square miles at an elevation of 981 feet. It sits where Interstates 35 and 80 meet, along Iowa Highway 141, and U.S. Route 6 forms its southern border with Clive. The 2020 census counted 45,580 people, which ranks Urbandale twelfth among Iowa cities, and the median age was 39.3.

sections.h2: How did Urbandale grow from a streetcar suburb?
sections.html:
Urbandale incorporated on April 16, 1917, as a streetcar suburb of Des Moines. Residents raised $2,000 for a two-room schoolhouse ready by 1916 so they would not have to join the Johnston school district, and four coal mines operated in the early years before closing by the end of the 1940s.

Streetcar service ended in 1951, and many DART bus routes now follow the old streetcar paths. Growth was fast after that:

  • 1920: 298 residents
  • 1950: 1,777 residents
  • 1970: 14,434 residents
  • 2000: 29,072 residents
  • 2020: 45,580 residents

Most of that growth came after 1950, so much of the city's housing is postwar, and owners are more likely to be dealing with mid-century or later systems than with century-old ones.

sections.h2: What do Census numbers say about Urbandale homes?
sections.html:
Urbandale is a high-income, mostly owner-occupied suburb. For 2020 to 2024 the Census Bureau lists the owner-occupied rate at 78.1 percent and the median value of owner-occupied homes at $335,500.

Measure (2020 to 2024)Urbandale
Median household income (2024 dollars)$112,795
Median gross rent$1,211
Persons per household2.64
Bachelor's degree or higher, ages 25+51.2%
Mean travel time to work18.9 minutes

With a median value that high, a house that needs a new roof or kitchen is a bigger gap between asking price and condition than it would be in a lower-value city, which is a common reason owners weigh an as-is sale.

sections.h2: What jobs and landmarks define Urbandale?
sections.html:
Finance and insurance lead the local economy at 17.9 percent of employment, followed by health care and social assistance at 11.8 percent and retail at 10.5 percent. Marsh and McLennan Companies is the largest named employer at roughly 1,000 to 1,100 workers, and the Urbandale Community School District, Quality Manufacturing Corp., MidAmerican Energy and the U.S. Postal Service each employ several hundred.

Business parks line the Urban Loop, a 12-mile stretch of I-35 and I-80, where a flyover ramp opened on October 16, 2020, at a cost of $65 million. The Multi-State Lottery Association is also based here.

Living History Farms is the best-known landmark. Pope John Paul II spoke there on October 4, 1979, to an estimated 350,000 people. The Olmsted Family Farmhouse, built in 1904, is the city's only site on the National Register of Historic Places.

sections.h2: How do Iowa weather and storms affect an Urbandale house?
sections.html:
Urbandale has a humid continental climate, with snowfall averaging 36.5 inches a season and annual precipitation of about 36.55 inches. Storm damage is part of the record: an F2 tornado hit on October 16, 1966, and an EF1 tornado on July 15, 2024.

If you are selling, the practical checklist is short:

  • Roof age and any hail or wind repair history.
  • Furnace and air conditioner age.
  • Basement moisture after heavy spring rain.

An insurance claim in the last few years may need to be explained to a buyer, so keep the paperwork.

The Urbandale Community School District runs six elementary schools, one middle school and Urbandale High School. Parts of the city are also served by the Dallas Center-Grimes, Des Moines, Johnston, Waukee and West Des Moines districts.

That mix means two neighbors a block apart may attend different districts. Buyers and agents ask about this early, so confirm your attendance district before you describe the property. Private options include Des Moines Christian School, which has more than 1,500 students, and St. Pius X Catholic School, opened in 1956.

sections.h2: What is it like to live in Urbandale day to day?
sections.html:
Urbandale runs a council-manager government with a mayor and five council members, each serving four-year terms. The city maintains 850 acres of parks and 54 miles of recreational trails that connect to other Des Moines-area trails.

For transit, DART Route 74 serves the northwestern business areas and connects to Windsor Heights and Valley West Mall. The Urban Loop business parks and interstate junction put many workplaces close to home. Park and trail access is worth mentioning if your house is near one.

sections.h2: What permits and fines should an Urbandale seller know about?
sections.html:
Urbandale says that any construction typically needs a building permit, and plumbing, mechanical and electrical work each need a separate permit. Even a portable shed needs zoning approval and must stay out of easements. Applications go through the city's online system or to Community Development at 3600 86th Street, and building services is at 515-278-3935.

Fees come from the schedule adopted for July 1, 2026:

ItemFee
Fence permit$30
Furnace or heater (mechanical)$15 per unit
Water heater (mechanical)$7 per unit
Work done without a permitDouble fee, building capped at $750
Tall weeds$50 admin fee plus mowing cost
Municipal infraction$750 first, $1,000 repeat

If past owners finished a basement or swapped a furnace without a permit, a buyer's inspector may ask about it, and fixing that before closing can take time.

sections.h2: How do property tax, transfer tax and disclosure work for an Urbandale sale?
sections.html:
Dallas County collects tax in two halves, due September 1 and March 1, and they turn delinquent after September 30 and March 31 with interest at 1.5 percent per month. The Dallas County Treasurer is in Adel at 800 Court Street, Suite 111. If your house is on the Polk County side, check with the Polk County Treasurer for its schedule.

Iowa's transfer tax is 80 cents for each $500 of value above the first $500. On the Urbandale median of $335,500, our math gives $536.00. The county recorder receives a declaration of value with the deed, and the closing agent files it.

Iowa Code 558A.4 describes what a seller's written disclosure covers, including significant structural defects and lead service lines.

sections.h2: What are the ways to sell a house in Urbandale?
sections.html:
• List with an agent: best for a house in good shape that can wait for showings and a buyer's loan.
  • Sell it yourself: saves commission and puts disclosure and negotiation on you.
  • Cash sale: a faster path with no repairs, which suits inherited, tenant-occupied or storm-damaged houses.

Get at least two written options and compare the net amount, the closing date and any contingencies.

faqs.q: Which county do I pay property tax to in Urbandale?
faqs.a: It depends on your parcel. Urbandale lies in both Polk and Dallas counties, so check your tax statement. Dallas County's dates are September 1 and March 1.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to replace a furnace or water heater in Urbandale?
faqs.a: Mechanical work needs a separate permit. The city's 2026 schedule lists $15 for a furnace or heater and $7 for a water heater, with a double fee for unpermitted work.

faqs.q: What is the median home value in Urbandale?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau reports $335,500 for owner-occupied homes from 2020 to 2024. Your own value can vary with age, size and condition.

faqs.q: Can I sell an Urbandale house that has storm damage?
faqs.a: Yes. You can sell as-is, but keep any insurance claim records. Urbandale had an EF1 tornado on July 15, 2024.

faqs.q: Which school district is my Urbandale house in?
faqs.a: The Urbandale Community School District is the main one, but parts of the city are served by Dallas Center-Grimes, Des Moines, Johnston, Waukee or West Des Moines. Confirm your address with the district.
